subject: Proposed MAP & commitment options for Acme Analytics - sizing, term, burst terms
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica.park@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed MAP & initial eval plan for Acme Analytics

Jessica —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Attached is a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and a lightweight GPU sizing workbook to make the pilot scoping easier. High level proposal:

- 2–4 week technical evaluation (pilot) to validate latency and throughput on a representative workload
- 30-day pilot SLA checkpoint: if pilot meets the SLAs we: 
  - apply pilot-success discount to first 3 months of reserved capacity overage,
  - move to a customer commit for reserved pool sizing (options below)
- Commitment/production ramp: 0–90 days ramp to steady state after PO sign

Key asks from your side for sizing and procurement:
- short sample traffic profile (qps, concurrency, typical sequence length)
- procurement timeline and PO routing (billing contact)

Initial reserve options (ballpark):
- Option A: 8 x A100-style nodes (higher per-card throughput) — good if you need lower latency for long-context workloads
- Option B: 16 x A10-style nodes (more parallel workers, cheaper per-token) — better for high-concurrency, shorter contexts

Pricing note: we can tier discounts by commit size and term length (12 vs 24 months). Burst usage is allowed under a clause (we typically allow 20–30% burst capacity for short windows at a premium multiplier). Exact numbers attached in the term sheet.

Attachments: Acme-MAP-v0.1.pdf (MAP draft), gpu-sizing-workbook.xlsx (workbook stub)

Proposed next step: Monica and I will draft an updated sizing recommendation after you share the traffic sample. If you can share procurement timing this week we can aim to finalize commercial terms by June 12 to align onboarding to early Q3.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.com]

From: Jessica Park <jessica.park@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: infra-team@acme-corp.com, legal@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP & initial eval plan for Acme Analytics

Karthik —

Thanks for the note and the MAP. A few clarifying questions before we share traffic samples:

1) Burst handling — does the pilot-success discount apply to burst overage or just to reserved baseline overage? Our platform can have short daily spikes (~45 minutes) that are 2–3x baseline during ETL windows.
2) Term length — what does Redwood recommend for customers who expect 2x growth in 12 months? Is a 12-month term with an optional top-up a common pattern?
3) Pricing granularity — do you price per GPU-hour or per reserved node? Can you share the math for the two sizing options so we can run procurement numbers (we need CAPEX vs OPEX implications)
4) Legal — I’ve CC'd our procurement and legal. They will want standard SLA language and audit log retention details.

Procurement timeline: we typically need 3–4 weeks for a PO once commercial terms are agreed (longer if new vendor onboarding is required). We can share a representative week of API logs by EOD tomorrow.

—Jessica Park
Director, Data Platform | Acme Analytics

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica.park@acme-corp.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposed MAP & initial eval plan for Acme Analytics (technical sizing notes)

Jessica —

I pulled together some quick guidance based on the usual tradeoffs. A few bullet points and an attached sample forecast (gpu-sizing-workbook.xlsx):

- If your spikes are short (<=60 min) and predictable, prefix/KV caching + burst capacity is the most cost-effective — keep a smaller steady reserved pool and rely on burst windows.
- If you have sustained high concurrency (100s concurrent users), more smaller cards (Option B: 16 x A10) are better because they increase concurrency per-dollar.
- For low-latency long-context use (10k tokens+), fewer higher-memory cards (Option A) reduce cross-node KV overhead and keep latency consistent.

Examples (rough):
- Option A: 8 nodes — covers 600 qps sustained for 512-token median sequences; lower tail latency for long queries
- Option B: 16 nodes — covers 1,200 qps for 256-token median sequences; cheaper per-token in sustained high-concurrency use

Operational items to lock in the MAP:
- Pilot SLA: 99th percentile latency threshold + error ceiling; if pilot misses SLA the MAP includes a remediation step before discounts trigger
- Burst clause: define burst window (daily/weekly), max burst percentage, billing multiplier for burst-hours (we propose 1.5x baseline for burst usage)

I put the sizing workbook with a few scenarios — we can run this live during a short call if that helps.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: gpu-sizing-workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica.park@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, legal@acme-corp.com
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial proposal: commit tiers, term options, and MAP milestones (Acme)

Jessica / Team —

Based on Monica’s notes and your expected spike patterns, here are two commercial paths we typically see and what they unlock in the MAP. Please review and flag any immediate concerns — we’d like to lock the MAP and term by Fri June 12 to hit your Q3 onboarding window.

Path 1 — 12-month commit (recommended conservative):
- Commit: reserve 12 nodes (midpoint between Options A/B) for 12 months
- Pricing: $X per GPU-hour (see term sheet attached)
- Discount schedule: 8% off list for the 12-node commit; additional 5% if pilot SLA passes within 30 days
- Burst: allowed up to 30% of committed capacity for up to 90 days per contract year at 1.5x baseline rate
- Benefit: faster procurement, lower near-term spend, ability to top-up if growth exceeds forecast

Path 2 — 24-month commit (aggressive cost optimization):
- Commit: reserve 12 nodes for 24 months
- Pricing: lower per-GPU-hour than Path 1 (additional 10% discount for 24-month term)
- Burst: 30% allowed; option to negotiate higher burst capacity if 24-month commit is signed
- Benefit: better unit economics (capex predictability)

Ancillary items:
- Pilot-success credit: If pilot meets MAP SLAs, Redwood will credit up to $Y of pilot usage against first invoice for reserved capacity.
- Upgrade/scale-down windows: customers can request a one-time scale-up or scale-down within the first 90 days with 30 days’ notice; scale-down credits are prorated and subject to a short notice fee.
- Audit & logs: 12 months of request + trace logs retained by default; extended retention available as an add-on.

Attached: redwood-term-sheet-v2.pdf (term sheet with pricing examples and sample SOW language)

Next steps (requested):
1) Acme to confirm preferred path (12 vs 24 months) and any must-have legal edits by June 10
2) Redwood to produce final SOW and PO-ready term sheet by June 12
3) Procurement sends PO; onboarding target: start of Q3

If you want, Rishi can join a short commercial call to walk through the math with your procurement team.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-term-sheet-v2.pdf]

From: legal@acme-corp.com
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jessica Park <jessica.park@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial proposal: commit tiers, term options, and MAP milestones (Acme)

Karthik / Jessica —

We reviewed the term sheet and have three principal asks before we can advance to PO: 

1) Auto-renew: remove automatic renewal or provide a 60-day opt-out written notice;
2) SLA credits: define concrete credit formula for SLA misses (percentage of monthly fees per missed metric);
3) Scale-down notice: reduce the scale-down notice to 14 days if the customer provides a documented forecast showing sustained lower utilization (procurement prefers shorter notice to adjust spend).

Please forward any standard amendments Redwood uses — we prefer to keep commercial terms simple and move quickly. Procurement lead time note: we will aim to issue PO within 3 weeks after commercial terms agreed but vendor onboarding can add 2 additional weeks.

Regards,
Acme Legal (on behalf of Acme Analytics)
[attachment: Acme-redlines-20260607.pdf (redlines)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica.park@acme-corp.com>, legal@acme-corp.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial proposal: commit tiers, term options, and MAP milestones (Acme) — confirmation

Team —

Thanks for the redlines and the speedy review. Summary of what Redwood can confirm so we can proceed to SOW/PO drafting: 

- Term & commit: Acme will proceed with Path 1 (12-month commit for 12 nodes) — we will include a one-time top-up option in the SOW.
- Pricing & discounts: Agreed to the 8% commit discount + 5% pilot-success discount. Final numbers will be in the SOW.
- Burst: 30% allowed at 1.5x baseline rate for up to 90 days/year; we will include an optional higher-burst addendum if Acme elects higher capacity at execution.
- Auto-renew: Redwood will remove automatic renewal and insert a 60-day non-renewal notice window (accepting Acme legal's request).
- SLA credits: Redwood to propose a specific credit table in the SOW (percentage-based) — Monica and I will include the exact formula.
- Scale-down notice: Redwood can shorten to 14 days if Acme provides the documented forecast described.

Action items:
- Redwood legal to incorporate Acme's redlines and return a PO-ready SOW by close of Tuesday, June 15.
- Monica to finalize the sizing workbook with the representative week of logs you promised and confirm the 12-node mapping to Option A/B mix.
- Rishi to schedule a 30-minute procurement walk-through next week to make sure the PO route is clear.

If that all looks good I’ll ask our legal team to produce the finalized SOW and term sheet for your signature. Appreciate the quick turnaround here — targeting a PO within three weeks after SOW finalization per your procurement note.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[signature]
